llm.summary: This hotel-search skill is mostly purpose-aligned, but it embeds a live proxy token and routes user travel queries through an external proxy service, so users should review it before installing.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and script consistently support Courtyard by Marriott hotel search, detail lookup, and package search; the external API calls are coherent with returning live prices and booking links.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions are narrowly scoped to Courtyard hotel queries and explicitly forbid fabricated hotel data; the data-flow section discloses that city/date/hotel query parameters are sent to a proxy service.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains only SKILL.md, a version file, and a Python helper script; no install-time execution, package installation, persistence hook, or local mutation mechanism was found. Network destinations are documented in prose rather than a separate permission manifest.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Network access is necessary for live hotel data, but the script hard-codes a shared proxy endpoint and authentication token, which is overbroad for a distributed skill and creates avoidable infrastructure and data-handling risk.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request local persistence or elevated privileges, but it does distribute a reusable proxy credential in source and sends it on every request.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending hotel search details such as destination, dates, hotel names, and review keywords to the listed proxy service. The publisher should move the proxy token out of the distributed source, rotate it, and document the proxy operator, retention behavior, and allowed endpoints.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Outbound requests for hotel search are expected and are disclosed in the data-flow section, but the artifact does not provide a stronger scoped permission or endpoint declaration beyond prose.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The hard-coded X-Proxy-Token in scripts/courtyard_hotel.py is not necessary to expose to all installers and is the main reason this needs Review rather than a benign pass.
[SQP-2] expected: Sending destination, hotel, date, and keyword parameters is necessary for live search and is disclosed, but the proxy's retention and handling guarantees are not independently supported by the artifact.
